RETENTION. The first 1.5 seconds must contain a visual question the viewer needs resolved. Plan an explicit beat every 2 to 3 seconds; nothing static may hold longer than that.

FORMAT LAW. Honour the grammar of the slow-motion destruction — its native framing, its edit rhythm, and the specific thing audiences expect from it. If the format loops, the last frame must match the first.

CAMERA. Compose 9:16 with the action in the safe centre band. Use a crane-up that starts at knee height and finishes above eye line on a 50mm normal, framing with frame-within-frame using foreground architecture.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with a large overhead octabox with a black flag killing the floor bounce; grade as a cinematic grade with a warm key and green-leaning ambient shadows. Specify the sound design in one clause — what the viewer hears in the first second decides whether they stay.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.
